All students pursuing a Bachelor of Business Administration, Bachelor of Arts in Economics, or Bachelor of Science in Materials Management and Logistics or Hospitality and Tourism Management from VCoBE, must apply for and be admitted to VCoBE before they are allowed to enroll in the Advanced Business Core and Major coursework for their degree. Schedule Type Lecture Grading Basis Standard Letter (A-F) Administrative Unit College of Business & Entrepreneurship

HOST 3370.name: Accounting and
HOST 3370.description: HOST 3370 Accounting and Financial Management for Hospitality Analysis of internal and external hospitality industry financial reports affect management decisions accounting and financial issues specifically related to the hospitality industry. Credits 3 Prerequisite HOST 1301 and FINA 3380. All students pursuing a Bachelor of Business Administration, Bachelor of Arts in Economics, or Bachelor of Science in Materials Management and Logistics or Hospitality and Tourism Management from VCoBE, must apply for and be admitted to VCoBE before they are allowed to enroll in the Advanced Business Core and Major coursework for their degree. Schedule Type Lecture Grading Basis Standard Letter (A-F) Administrative Unit College of Business & Entrepreneurship

HOST 4310.name: Restaurant
HOST 4310.description: HOST 4310 Restaurant Management Operations Managing restaurant operations for high-level service and quality including food and beverage decision and production, personnel and facilities. Includes a laboratory. Credits 3 Prerequisite HOST 1301 , HOST 3310 , and Junior Standing. All students pursuing a Bachelor of Business Administration, Bachelor of Arts in Economics, or Bachelor of Science in Materials Management and Logistics or Hospitality and Tourism Management from VCoBE, must apply for and be admitted to VCoBE before they are allowed to enroll in the Advanced Business Core and Major coursework for their degree. Schedule Type Lecture/Lab Grading Basis Standard Letter (A-F) Administrative Unit College of Business & Entrepreneurship

HOST 4312.name: Catering
HOST 4312.description: HOST 4312 Catering Management The management of catering operations including food and beverage preparation, menu planning, service and deals. Credits 3 Prerequisite HOST 1301 , HOST 3310 , and Junior Standing. All students pursuing a Bachelor of Business Administration, Bachelor of Arts in Economics, or Bachelor of Science in Materials Management and Logistics or Hospitality and Tourism Management from VCoBE, must apply for and be admitted to VCoBE before they are allowed to enroll in the Advanced Business Core and Major coursework for their degree. Schedule Type Lecture Grading Basis Standard Letter (A-F) Administrative Unit College of Business & Entrepreneurship

HOST 4314.name: Wine &
HOST 4314.description: HOST 4314 Wine & Beverage Appreciation Introduction to wines, beers, and distilled spirits in the dining experience. Includes standards of quality, processing storage, service, and recommending food combinations with wine and spirits. Credits 3 Prerequisite Junior Standing. Must be of legal drinking age. All students pursuing a Bachelor of Business Administration, Bachelor of Arts in Economics, or Bachelor of Science in Materials Management and Logistics or Hospitality and Tourism Management from VCoBE, must apply for and be admitted to VCoBE before they are allowed to enroll in the Advanced Business Core and Major coursework for their degree. Schedule Type Lecture/Lab Grading Basis Standard Letter (A-F) Administrative Unit College of Business & Entrepreneurship

HOST 4320.name: Tourism
HOST 4320.description: HOST 4320 Tourism Destination Marketing Concepts and strategies related to the strategic management of destinations for tourism including ecotourism. Credits 3 Prerequisite HOST 1301 and Junior Standing. All students pursuing a Bachelor of Business Administration, Bachelor of Arts in Economics, or Bachelor of Science in Materials Management and Logistics or Hospitality and Tourism Management from VCoBE, must apply for and be admitted to VCoBE before they are allowed to enroll in the Advanced Business Core and Major coursework for their degree. Schedule Type Lecture Grading Basis Standard Letter (A-F) Administrative Unit College of Business & Entrepreneurship

HOST 4330.name: Advanced
HOST 4330.description: HOST 4330 Advanced Lodging Management Managing and critically evaluating all aspects of lodging operations for quality and profitability. Includes laboratory. Credits 3 Prerequisite HOST 1301 , HOST 3330 , and Junior Standing. All students pursuing a Bachelor of Business Administration, Bachelor of Arts in Economics, or Bachelor of Science in Materials Management and Logistics or Hospitality and Tourism Management from VCoBE, must apply for and be admitted to VCoBE before they are allowed to enroll in the Advanced Business Core and Major coursework for their degree. Schedule Type Lecture Grading Basis Standard Letter (A-F) Administrative Unit College of Business & Entrepreneurship

HOST 4370.name: Hospitality
HOST 4370.description: HOST 4370 Hospitality Analytics and Revenue Management Revenue management practices in the hospitality industry, including capacity management, revenue forecasting, and pricing strategies. Credits 3 Prerequisite HOST 3310 , HOST 3370 , and Junior Standing. All students pursuing a Bachelor of Business Administration, Bachelor of Arts in Economics, or Bachelor of Science in Materials Management and Logistics or Hospitality and Tourism Management from VCoBE, must apply for and be admitted to VCoBE before they are allowed to enroll in the Advanced Business Core and Major coursework for their degree. Schedule Type Lecture Grading Basis Standard Letter (A-F) Administrative Unit College of Business & Entrepreneurship

HOST 4390.name: Hospitality
HOST 4390.description: HOST 4390 Hospitality Strategic Planning and Analysis Strategic-decision making in hospitality and tourism organizations. Feasibility study required. To be taken in the final semester before graduation. Credits 3 Prerequisite All students pursuing a Bachelor of Business Administration, Bachelor of Arts in Economics, or Bachelor of Science in Materials Management and Logistics or Hospitality and Tourism Management from VCoBE, must apply for and be admitted to VCoBE before they are allowed to enroll in the Advanced Business Core and Major coursework for their degree. HPRS 3301.name: Introduction to the
HPRS 3301.description: HPRS 3301 Introduction to the Evolving Healthcare System Introduces the student to the organizational structure of the U.S. Health Care system. Provides historical perspective to the system evolution from institutional-based to population based are to cost-aware values. Describes the financing mechanisms, primary providers and secondary providers, and consumers of healthcare. Discusses how technology affects the politics of the system. Discusses the health care system along the Texas-Mexico borders and how cultural influences impacts health care delivery. Credits 3 Schedule Type Lecture Grading Basis Standard Letter (A-F) Administrative Unit Department of Health and Biomedical Sciences Offered As scheduled

HPRS 3302.name: Medical
HPRS 3302.description: HPRS 3302 Medical Law/Ethics for the Health Professional Describes the laws and ethical standards that apply to allied health practitioners. Uses case presentations and develops methods for solving legal and or ethical and cultural dilemmas. Discuss pertinent legal cases involving allied health practitioners. Credits 3 Schedule Type Lecture Grading Basis Standard Letter (A-F) Administrative Unit Department of Health and Biomedical Sciences Offered As scheduled

HPRS 3309.name: Leading and
HPRS 3309.description: HPRS 3309 Leading and Managing the Healthcare Team Discusses the concepts of leadership within the context of allied health. Prepares the learner to use problem solving methods to effectively supervise and lead subordinates in a health care setting. Focuses on the economics of managed care, how continuous quality improvement relates to cost-effective care. Develops skills and values necessary for effective teamwork. Credits 3 Schedule Type Lecture Grading Basis Standard Letter (A-F) Administrative Unit Department of Health and Biomedical Sciences Offered As scheduled

HPRS 3313.name: Physical and
HPRS 3313.description: HPRS 3313 Physical and Mental Health Throughout the Lifespan This course provides concepts of growth, development, and mental health through human stages of life, focusing on biological/genetic and environmental influences on the cognitive, physical, and socio-emotional/psychological developmental areas. Course concepts are demonstrated by applying principles and theories through discussion of current lifespan issues. Credits 3 Schedule Type Lecture Grading Basis Standard Letter (A-F) Administrative Unit Department of Health and Biomedical Sciences Offered As scheduled

HPRS 3316.name: Nutrition
HPRS 3316.description: HPRS 3316 Nutrition Concepts for Allied Health Practitioners This course is designed to emphasize the importance of nutrition in maintaining health and wellness. The effect of diet on specific diseases will be explored. Students will practice methods of diet recording and evaluation. Credits 3 Schedule Type Lecture Grading Basis Standard Letter (A-F) Administrative Unit Department of Health and Biomedical Sciences Offered As scheduled

HPRS 3319.name: Compliance and
HPRS 3319.description: HPRS 3319 Compliance and Risk Management for Health Science In this course students will begin to understand, identify and evaluate risk as a mean to reduce injury to patients, staff members, and visitors within an organization and understand how to work proactively and reactively to either prevent incident or to minimize the damage following an event in a healthcare setting. Requirements and principles of compliance in a health care setting will be introduced. Credits 3 Schedule Type Lecture Grading Basis Standard Letter (A-F) Administrative Unit Department of Health and Biomedical Sciences

HPRS 3320.name: Patient
HPRS 3320.description: HPRS 3320 Patient Education in Health Sciences This course will cover adult learning theories and concepts to help learners develop appropriate teaching materials and programs for patients and their families that enhance client knowledge and skills for health promotion and recovery. Credits 3 Schedule Type Lecture Grading Basis Standard Letter (A-F) Administrative Unit Department of Health and Biomedical Sciences Offered As scheduled

HPRS 3324.name: Teaching in the
HPRS 3324.description: HPRS 3324 Teaching in the Health Sciences This course will provide an introduction to the principles of teaching to include planning, implementation, assessment and evaluation in health career education. Credits 3 Schedule Type Lecture Grading Basis Standard Letter (A-F) Administrative Unit Department of Health and Biomedical Sciences Offered As scheduled

HPRS 4300.name: Pharmacology for
HPRS 4300.description: HPRS 4300 Pharmacology for Health Professional This course is designed to provide concepts central to the study of pharmacology, the interaction between chemical substances and living tissues as these relate to the allied health professionals' clinical settings. Human systems and common pathophysiology will be reviewed, and the use of common medication regimens will be presented. Successful students will demonstrate their grasp of the concepts inherent in pharmacological treatments in the clinical arena or in related drug research by applying these concepts on course assignments. Credits 3 Schedule Type Lecture Grading Basis Standard Letter (A-F) Administrative Unit Department of Health and Biomedical Sciences Offered As scheduled

HPRS 4301.name: Introduction to
HPRS 4301.description: HPRS 4301 Introduction to Health Data Utilization This course is designed to introduce the student to health information management profession, healthcare data delivery systems, along with health information functions, purpose, and users.  The student will become familiar with data content and standards, as well as information protection.  Learners will understand informatics and data use, as well as revenue management and compliance. Credits 3 Schedule Type Lecture Grading Basis Standard Letter (A-F) Administrative Unit Department of Health and Biomedical Sciences Offered As scheduled

HPRS 4302.name: Continuous
HPRS 4302.description: HPRS 4302 Continuous Quality Improvement Provides basic principles of CQI and its application in health care environments. Provides knowledge, skills, and tools necessary to implement, facilitate, and coordinate CQI activities. This requires experience in a healthcare setting and moderate computer skills including creating spreadsheets, charts and graphs. Credits 3 Schedule Type Lecture Grading Basis Standard Letter (A-F) Administrative Unit Department of Health and Biomedical Sciences Offered As scheduled

HPRS 4305.name: Public
HPRS 4305.description: HPRS 4305 Public Health Concepts This course is designed to provide an introduction to public health concepts which include: history, border health issues, function and context of public health, community health, health systems, improving the health of communities through research, prevention, disease detection, and healthy lifestyle promotion. Credits 3 Schedule Type Lecture Grading Basis Standard Letter (A-F) Administrative Unit Department of Health and Biomedical Sciences

HPRS 4309.name: Methods in
HPRS 4309.description: HPRS 4309 Methods in Evidenced-Based Healthcare This course incorporates basic research methods, processes and models in analyzing research studies and incorporating current quality and ethical research standards.  Students will learn to make informed decisions and critically evaluate research.   Students will practice research methods, including literature search, hypothesis generation and testing, sampling theory, research design, data analysis and report-writing. Credits 3 Schedule Type Lecture Grading Basis Standard Letter (A-F) Administrative Unit Department of Health and Biomedical Sciences Offered As scheduled

HPRS 4310.name: Introduction to
HPRS 4310.description: HPRS 4310 Introduction to Epidemiology for Health Science This course will provide an introduction to epidemiological principles and concepts which include: history, vocabulary, methods, design, interpretation, and evaluation of epidemiological research. The emphasis is on public health practice of epidemiology, evidence-based practice and will include border health issues. Credits 3 Prerequisite MATH 1314 or MATH 1414 or MATH 1342 or MATH 1343 or MATH 1388 or MATH 2412 or MATH 2413 . Schedule Type Lecture Grading Basis Standard Letter (A-F) Administrative Unit Department of Health and Biomedical Sciences Offered As scheduled
HPRS 4310.prereq_raw: MATH 1314 or MATH 1414 or MATH 1342 or MATH 1343 or MATH 1388 or MATH 2412 or MATH 2413

HPRS 4312.name: Applied
HPRS 4312.description: HPRS 4312 Applied Pathophysiology This course will review disease processes and how human systems are affected. Emphasis is placed on prevention and treatment of diseases. Students will differentiate between normal and abnormal physiology and make informed decisions using critical thinking and problem solving. Credits 3 Prerequisite BIOL 1406 or BIOL 2401 , or permission of the instructor. Schedule Type Lecture Grading Basis Standard Letter (A-F) Administrative Unit Department of Health and Biomedical Sciences Offered As scheduled
HPRS 4312.prereq_raw: BIOL 1406 or BIOL 2401 , or permission of the instructor

HPRS 4315.name: Health
HPRS 4315.description: HPRS 4315 Health Disparities This course is designed to introduce the inequalities that occur in the provision of healthcare and access to healthcare including: racial and cultural factors, poor access to healthcare, socioeconomic status, environmental exposures, poor health literacy, individual and behavioral factors. Will include inequities specific to border health. Credits 3 Prerequisite HPRS 4305 . Schedule Type Lecture Grading Basis Standard Letter (A-F) Administrative Unit Department of Health and Biomedical Sciences

HPRS 4316.name: Applied
HPRS 4316.description: HPRS 4316 Applied Medical Microbiology Students in Medical Microbiology study the morphology and physiology of microbes and the relationship between microbes and health maintenance. Emphasis is placed on the role of microbes in infectious diseases. Credits 3 Prerequisite BIOL 1406 or BIOL 2401 , or permission of the instructor. Schedule Type Lecture Grading Basis Standard Letter (A-F) Administrative Unit Department of Health and Biomedical Sciences Offered As scheduled
HPRS 4316.prereq_raw: BIOL 1406 or BIOL 2401 , or permission of the instructor

HPRS 4320.name: Border
HPRS 4320.description: HPRS 4320 Border Health Issues This course examines issues in border health care specifically on the U.S.-Mexico border, social, cultural, political and economic factors are explored in relation to health care delivery and policy formulation along the border. Health care strategies and programs are evaluated using research approaches. Credits 3 Schedule Type Lecture Grading Basis Standard Letter (A-F) Administrative Unit Department of Health and Biomedical Sciences

HPRS 4334.name: Issues and
HPRS 4334.description: HPRS 4334 Issues and Trends in Health Care This course will address current events, issues and attitudes pertinent to health care. Credits 3 Schedule Type Lecture Grading Basis Standard Letter (A-F) Administrative Unit Department of Health and Biomedical Sciences Offered As scheduled

HRPT 2303.name: Medical
HRPT 2303.description: HRPT 2303 Medical Terminology This course is designed to introduce the student to analysis techniques and to correct spelling and pronunciation of medical terms. The student will have the opportunity to learn a medical vocabulary, develop skills in recognizing medical terms by analyzing their elements and relating them to the corresponding anatomical site. Credits 3 Schedule Type Lecture Grading Basis Standard Letter (A-F) Administrative Unit Department of Health and Biomedical Sciences Offered Fall/Spring/Summer

HSIN 3310.name: Health
HSIN 3310.description: HSIN 3310 Health Data Science The course introduces current and emerging practices in health data science. Learners will gain knowledge and skills related to the scientific study of the creation, validation, and transformation of data to create meaning. The goal of the course is for learners to deepen their understanding of the interprofessional, multi-disciplinary nature of the skill sets and expertise required for health data scientists. Credits 3 Prerequisite Credit or registration in HPRS 4301 . Schedule Type Lecture Grading Basis Standard Letter (A-F) Administrative Unit Department of Health and Biomedical Sciences Offered Spring

HSIN 3320.name: Health
HSIN 3320.description: HSIN 3320 Health Data Research and Analytics This course introduces the foundations of health data research and the analytics to transition data from information to knowledge and actionable wisdom. Learners will be familiarized with national data standards, data sources, data management, and approaches to analytics relevant to healthcare data. Credits 3 Prerequisite Credit or registration in HPRS 4301 . Schedule Type Lecture Grading Basis Standard Letter (A-F) Administrative Unit Department of Health and Biomedical Sciences Offered Fall semester

HSIN 4310.name: Data
HSIN 4310.description: HSIN 4310 Data Privacy and Security in Healthcare This course will introduce the principles of the Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act (HIPAA) concerning Privacy and Security Rules and other federal, state, and local laws governing the privacy, security, and exchange of healthcare information. Learners will gain the skills and knowledge to understand cybersecurity threats, threat actors, cybersecurity risk management best practices, digital health innovation, laws, and regulations applicable to electronic health records, as well as techniques that are being used to build cybersecurity awareness. Credits 3 Prerequisite Credit or registration in HPRS 4301 . Schedule Type Lecture Grading Basis Standard Letter (A-F) Administrative Unit Department of Health and Biomedical Sciences Offered Spring

INDS 2190.name: Humanities and
INDS 2190.description: INDS 2190 Humanities and Service Learning INDS 2190 provides students the opportunity to develop a student-centered and student-directed experiential/service-learning project that is completed in relation to work in INDS 2390 , Humanities in the World. Students will draw from the readings and discussion of INDS 2390 and use this knowledge as a foundation to formulate their projects. Credits 1 Corequisite INDS 2390 . Schedule Type Lecture Grading Basis Standard Letter (A-F) Administrative Unit Department of Literature and Cultural Studies Offered As scheduled

INDS 2390.name: Humanities in the
INDS 2390.description: INDS 2390 Humanities in the World INDS 2390 examines art, architecture, literature, and film in a social context. It further explores the place of the work of art and literature in the world as it draws from reading across the disciplines. Students will read and discuss a broad range of materials to gain a global and cross-cultural perspective on the Humanities. Credits 3 Schedule Type Lecture Grading Basis Standard Letter (A-F) Administrative Unit Department of Literature and Cultural Studies Offered As scheduled

INFS 1001.name: Computer
INFS 1001.description: INFS 1001 Computer Proficiency Utilizing Blackboard, new incoming students are informed of appropriate university and degree-related announcements, activities, and responsibilities, and are asses for computer proficiency. Credits 0 Schedule Type Lecture Grading Basis Credit/No Credit Administrative Unit Department of Information Systems Offered As scheduled

INFS 1301.name: Computer
INFS 1301.description: INFS 1301 Computer Information Systems This course serves as an introduction to the primary components of a business computer system and to the primary application software packages used to increase productivity of business professionals. These topics will be reinforced with microcomputer laboratory exercises. Students failing to demonstrate computer proficiency who wish to take advanced business courses in the must take this course. Credits 3 Schedule Type Lecture Grading Basis Standard Letter (A-F) Administrative Unit Department of Information Systems Offered Fall/Spring/Summer

INFS 2300.name: Data
INFS 2300.description: INFS 2300 Data Modeling Management Tools Students taking this course will learn to build, enhance, and manipulate business spreadsheets; to make reports and charts; to conduct what-if analyses; and to complete advanced analyses in Excel. They will also be introduced to the steps involved in building, maintaining, and enhancing databases, and working with tables, queries forms and reports. They will learn how spreadsheets and Microsoft databases can share information with other Microsoft programs. Credits 3 Schedule Type Lecture Grading Basis Standard Letter (A-F) TCCNS BCIS 1305 Administrative Unit Department of Information Systems Offered Fall/Spring/Summer

INFS 3300.name: Internship in
INFS 3300.description: INFS 3300 Internship in Information Systems and Business Analytics This course is designed to give students an opportunity to gain real-world experience in their chosen career field by working with a participating employing firm or organization. The students will be supervised by a faculty member acting as a liaison between the employing organization and the academic department to assure compliance with specific learning and experience requirements. Credits 3 Prerequisite Six credit hours in ( INFS 3308 , INFS 3310 , INFS 3320 , INFS 3325 , INFS 3330 , INFS 3333 , INFS 3335 , INFS 3336 , INFS 3338 , INFS 3375 , INFS 3395 , INFS 4308 , INFS 4312, INFS 4330 , INFS 4340 , INFS 4391 , INFS 4395 , INFS 4397 , INFS 4399 or QUMT 4343 ) with a "C" or better; approval by the department chair.  All students pursuing a Bachelor of Business Administration, Bachelor of Arts in Economics, or Bachelor of Science in Materials Management and Logistics from VCoBE, must apply for and be admitted to VCoBE before they are allowed to enroll in the Advanced Business Core and Major coursework for their degree. Schedule Type Practicum Grading Basis Standard Letter (A-F) Administrative Unit Department of Information Systems Offered Fall/Spring/Summer

INFS 3308.name: Business
INFS 3308.description: INFS 3308 Business Information Infrastructure This course introduces students to the basic concepts of computing and information technology infrastructure components in the context of the contemporary business environment. Topics include computer architecture, traditional packaged and open-source software, operating systems, cloud computing, virtualization, web services and multimedia, and business impacts and strategies for these technologies. Credits 3 Prerequisite Sophomore Standing. All students pursuing a Bachelor of Business Administration, Bachelor of Arts in Economics, or Bachelor of Science in Hospitality and Tourism Management from VCoBE, must apply for and be admitted to VCoBE before they can enroll in the Advanced Business Core and Major coursework for their degree.  Prerequisites are waived for the students pursuing a Bachelor of Science in Cyber Security or a minor in Cyber Security. Schedule Type Lecture Grading Basis Standard Letter (A-F) Administrative Unit Department of Information Systems Offered Fall/Spring/Summer

INFS 3310.name: Introduction to
INFS 3310.description: INFS 3310 Introduction to Business Programming Students will be introduced to developing business applications using modern programming languages. Topics include fundamentals of logic development and implementation, user interface design, data controls, and systems integration. Students will understand terminology and principles of programming; produce coding plans for problem statements, sample test cases, and pseudo-code; and be able to design, develop, test, and implement working application programs for given business problem specifications. Credits 3 Prerequisite Sophomore Standing. All students pursuing a Bachelor of Business Administration, Bachelor of Arts in Economics, or Bachelor of Science in Hospitality and Tourism Management from VCoBE, must apply for and be admitted to VCoBE before they can enroll in the Advanced Business Core and Major coursework for their degree. Schedule Type Lecture Grading Basis Standard Letter (A-F) Administrative Unit Department of Information Systems Offered Fall/Spring

INFS 3320.name: Organizational
INFS 3320.description: INFS 3320 Organizational Information Assurance This course covers concepts of information assurance in enterprises. Students will learn how to: demonstrate understanding of the dimensions of organizational information assurance; evaluate meaningful metrics to measure the quality of information assurance, and set appropriate priorities and policies; measure security risk and present plans for loss prevention, incident response, mitigation strategies, and recovery of business information assets after an incident; improve communication to business owners and security teams, including legal and public relations implications of business information security and privacy issues. Credits 3 Prerequisite Advanced standing; INFS 3308 and INFS 3310 with a "C" or better, or permission of the instructor. All students  pursuing a Bachelor of Business Administration, Bachelor of Arts in Economics, or Bachelor of Science in Materials Management and Logistics from VCoBE, must apply for and be admitted to VCoBE before they are allowed to enroll in the Advanced Business Core and Major coursework for their degree. Schedule Type Lecture Grading Basis Standard Letter (A-F) Administrative Unit Department of Information Systems Offered Fall (only)
INFS 3320.prereq_raw: Advanced standing; INFS 3308 and INFS 3310 with a "C" or better, or permission of the instructor

INFS 3325.name: Introduction to
INFS 3325.description: INFS 3325 Introduction to Python Programming for Business Analytics This course will introduce students to Python for Business Analytics. Students will address business problems by applying the capabilities of Python, including scripts and analytics libraries, to carry out analyses in statistics, data modeling, and machine learning. Students will learn to design solutions, and then apply serial, functional, and object-oriented approaches to coding to implement their designs in Python. Credits 3 Prerequisite All students pursuing a Bachelor of Business Administration, Bachelor of Arts in Economics, or Bachelor of Science in Materials Management and Logistics from VCoBE, must apply for and be admitted to VCoBE before they are allowed to enroll in the Advanced Business Core and Major coursework for their degree. Schedule Type Lecture Grading Basis Standard Letter (A-F) Administrative Unit Department of Information Systems Offered As schedule
INFS 3325.prereq_raw: All students pursuing a Bachelor of Business Administration, Bachelor of Arts in Economics, or Bachelor of Science in Materials Management and Logistics from VCoBE, must apply for and be admitted to VCoBE before they are allowed to enroll in the Advanced Business Core and Major coursework for their degree

INFS 3333.name: Advanced
INFS 3333.description: INFS 3333 Advanced Spreadsheet Modeling Accessible to almost anyone, the spreadsheet is a simple, yet powerful data analytic tool used by major corporations and small businesses alike. Users may develop spreadsheet models by themselves to determine key measures of success at operational, managerial, and strategic levels. This course introduces advanced Excel formulas, techniques, and procedures for spreadsheet modeling (including but not limited to macros, automation, Visual Basic for Applications (VBA), Pivot table, and PowerPivot to Excel) to harness its power in data sensemaking and decision support. The technical skills and managerial capabilities acquired will be useful to careers in the financial, medical, retailing, manufacturing, transportation, and construction fields, to name but a few. Credits 3 Prerequisite INFS 2300 or department approval. All students pursuing a Bachelor of Business Administration, or Bachelor of Arts in Economics from VCoBE, must apply for and be admitted to VCoBE before they are allowed to enroll in the Advanced Business Core and Major coursework for their degree. Schedule Type Lecture Grading Basis Standard Letter (A-F) Administrative Unit Department of Information Systems

INFS 3335.name: Database
INFS 3335.description: INFS 3335 Database Management This course is an introduction to the foundations of database technology. Basic knowledge of data structures, normalization of data, and data modeling will be included. Relational, hierarchical, and network models will be covered. The student will be introduced to the rudiments of the construction of database schema via laboratory experiences stressing application development through advanced programming techniques and SQL. Credits 3 Prerequisite Advanced standing. All students pursuing a Bachelor of Business Administration, Bachelor of Arts in Economics, or Bachelor of Science in Materials Management and Logistics from VCoBE, must apply for and be admitted to VCoBE before they are allowed to enroll in the Advanced Business Core and Major coursework for their degree. Schedule Type Lecture Grading Basis Standard Letter (A-F) Administrative Unit Department of Information Systems Offered Fall/Spring

INFS 3336.name: Systems
INFS 3336.description: INFS 3336 Systems Analysis This course examines the analysis of business information systems and their redesign through automated applications. Students will learn the nature of information needs and the role of information systems in organizations. Using a variety of information systems development approaches and problem-solving tools, student will initiate, plan and analyze a real-life project within an organization. Team projects will result in a system proposal. Credits 3 Prerequisite Advanced standing; INFS 3308 and INFS 3310 with a "C" or better. All students  pursuing a Bachelor of Business Administration, Bachelor of Arts in Economics, or Bachelor of Science in Materials Management and Logistics from VCoBE, must apply for and be admitted to VCoBE before they are allowed to enroll in the Advanced Business Core and Major coursework for their degree. Schedule Type Lecture Grading Basis Standard Letter (A-F) Administrative Unit Department of Information Systems Offered Fall (only)
INFS 3336.prereq_raw: Advanced standing; INFS 3308 and INFS 3310 with a "C" or better

INFS 3338.name: Computer
INFS 3338.description: INFS 3338 Computer Networks and the Internet This course provides knowledge of the fundamental concepts of data communication and networking to the students. Topics include Application layer, Physical layer, Data Link Layer, Network Layer, and Transport Layer. In addition, classification of network technologies is explained, including wired and wireless local area networks, wide area networks, and backbone networks. Key concepts underlying network management and network design are emphasized. Credits 3 Prerequisite Advanced standing; INFS 3308 and INFS 3310 with a "C" or better. All students  pursuing a Bachelor of Business Administration, Bachelor of Arts in Economics, or Bachelor of Science in Materials Management and Logistics from VCoBE, must apply for and be admitted to VCoBE before they are allowed to enroll in the Advanced Business Core and Major coursework for their degree. Schedule Type Lecture Grading Basis Standard Letter (A-F) Administrative Unit Department of Information Systems Offered Fall/Spring
INFS 3338.prereq_raw: Advanced standing; INFS 3308 and INFS 3310 with a "C" or better

INFS 3375.name: Data
INFS 3375.description: INFS 3375 Data Visualization This course focuses on developing technical and creative skills to transform data into visual reports for producing a shared understanding. Students will learn to use software to organize and visualize data, with an emphasis on applying best practices in data visualization and design principles to produce clear, polished interactive graphs and dashboards that engender an insight, message, or recommendation distilled from the data. Students will use data visualization and dashboarding software and develop transferable skills that can apply to the most common software packages in the field. Students will have the opportunity to gain hands-on experience in data visualization and become familiar with data visualization techniques for data storytelling. Credits 3 Prerequisite All students pursuing a Bachelor of Business Administration, Bachelor of Arts in Economics, or Bachelor of Science in Materials Management and Logistics from VCoBE, must apply for and be admitted to VCoBE before they are allowed to enroll in the Advanced Business Core and Major coursework for their degree. Schedule Type Lecture Grading Basis Standard Letter (A-F) Administrative Unit Department of Information Systems Offered Once a year
INFS 3375.prereq_raw: All students pursuing a Bachelor of Business Administration, Bachelor of Arts in Economics, or Bachelor of Science in Materials Management and Logistics from VCoBE, must apply for and be admitted to VCoBE before they are allowed to enroll in the Advanced Business Core and Major coursework for their degree

INFS 3380.name: Global
INFS 3380.description: INFS 3380 Global Information Technology The purpose of this course is to investigate the role of information technologies in multinational settings. This course will examine the international business environment and how information systems and technology can be effectively utilized in multinational environments. Credits 3 Prerequisite Advanced standing; MGMT 3361 with a "C" or better; or permission of the instructor. All students  pursuing a Bachelor of Business Administration, Bachelor of Arts in Economics, or Bachelor of Science in Materials Management and Logistics from VCoBE, must apply for and be admitted to VCoBE before they are allowed to enroll in the Advanced Business Core and Major coursework for their degree.  Prerequisites are waived for the students pursuing a Bachelor of Science in Cyber Security. Schedule Type Lecture Grading Basis Standard Letter (A-F) Administrative Unit Department of International Business and Entrepreneurship Offered Fall/Spring/Summer

This course focuses on data quality and business intelligence through data wrangling and data warehousing. Students will work on raw data preprocessing, business analysis, architectural design, dimensional modeling, data loading/extraction, and online analytical processing. The knowledge and skills acquired can be applied to various industries, such as healthcare, banking, retailing, logistics, and manufacturing. Credits 3 Prerequisite INFS 3335 . This course leads the students through a complete project life cycle, from requirements analysis and project definition to start-up, reviews, and phase-out. The role of the project manager as team leader is examined together with important techniques for controlling project costs, schedules, and performance. Lectures, case studies, a research project, and group discussions are combined to develop the skills needed by project managers in today's business environments. The course introduces students to data mining that uses Python and R programming languages. The course discusses both supervised machine learning classification and prediction techniques including decision trees, neural networks, time series analysis, and unsupervised machine learning techniques such as clustering and association analysis. INFS 4381.description: INFS 4381 Online Presence for the Arts INFS 4381 , Online Presence for the Arts, will be a hands-on, technologically-oriented course providing students with the tools and skills to design, build, protect, and maintain digital arts information and artifacts on the Internet. Both students whose primary interest is the arts, and those who are aiming at careers as IT professionals, can benefit from this course. Students will study examples of artists online with individual websites, sites for posting content, social media presence and career websites, and go on to create their own portfolio establishing a digital online presence. Topics will include: web and multimedia design principles, HTML and CSS, website hosting, characteristics of digital information goods, traditional and creative commons licensing, translating physical artifacts to digital forms, watermarking, digital rights management, intellectual property laws and practices, arts e-commerce, and generative AI. INHS 1301.name: Introduction to
INHS 1301.description: INHS 1301 Introduction to Health Science & Professions This course will provide an overview of health science careers, introduce the importance of interprofessional healthcare practices, and assist with career planning and selecting an appropriate major/minor. The course will address critical soft skills including communication competency, professionalism, embracing diversity, effective critical thinking, and the personal qualities of a healthcare worker. The history, currently emerging and future state of health care in the U.S. will be introduced. And the basics of patient safety and infection control. Credits 3 Schedule Type Lecture Grading Basis Standard Letter (A-F) Administrative Unit Department of Health Sciences

INHS 2301.name: The
INHS 2301.description: INHS 2301 The Practice of Health Science This course will provide an overview of health systems science and introduce the student learner to systems thinking in health care, the health care delivery system and structures, the use of clinical informatics, population health concepts, and health care law and ethics. This course will also explore the role of health care policy and the use of assessment in health science student learning. Credits 3 Prerequisite Grade of "C" or better in INHS 1301 . INHS 3305.name: Global
INHS 3305.description: INHS 3305 Global Health Dynamics This course explores the political, economic, and cultural processes of globalization and their impact on population health and healthcare systems globally. Students will examine factors that either promote or hinder health equity within an ethical framework grounded in healthcare initiatives, human rights, and social justice. Key topics include pressing global health issues such as HIV/AIDS, human trafficking, infectious diseases, reproductive health, and the social determinants of health. Emphasis is placed on developing practical skills in healthcare interventions and cultural competence to address global health challenges. Credits 3 Prerequisite Grade of "C" or better in INHS 1301 and INHS 2301 . Schedule Type Lecture Grading Basis Standard Letter (A-F) Administrative Unit Department of Health Sciences Offered As Scheduled

INHS 3315.description: INHS 3315 Environmental Health Literacy for Empowerment Emerging issues in environmental health literacy are examined using current literature and case studies. This course emphasizes the role of environmental factorsâsuch as pollution, water quality, and climateâin the disease process and health outcomes. Students will learn to communicate complex health information effectively, empowering patients to make informed health decisions. Upon critically evaluating environmental health data, students will develop literacy strategies that support patient engagement, education, and preventive practices. Credits 3 Prerequisite Grade of "C" or better in INHS 1301 and INHS 2301 . Schedule Type Lecture Grading Basis Standard Letter (A-F) Administrative Unit Department of Health Sciences
INHS 3315.prereq_raw: Grade of "C" or better in INHS 1301 and INHS 2301

INHS 3325.name: Healthcare
INHS 3325.description: INHS 3325 Healthcare Leadership Structure and Professionalism This course will provide a comprehensive overview of healthcare leadership structure in healthcare systems in the US. This course covers concepts and methodologies on how professionalism makes a whole new way of leadership to develop robust and long-lasting high-quality patient care delivery systems. The course offers core concepts of leadership, leadership styles, and how to implement some of the most common methods of solid leadership in US Healthcare today. Credits 3 Prerequisite Junior classification. Schedule Type Lecture Grading Basis Standard Letter (A-F) Administrative Unit Department of Health Sciences

INHS 3347.name: Health
INHS 3347.description: INHS 3347 Health Science Information Management and Analysis This course examines the function and purpose of information management in the improvement of health science practice. Content is comprised of instruments and practices necessary for effective information flow among healthcare facilities. Mobile health technology is introduced for applicability, opportunity, and appropriate use. The interpretation and analysis of data within health records are critically analyzed for quality, interoperability, security, and retrieval. Credits 3 Schedule Type Lecture Grading Basis Standard Letter (A-F) Administrative Unit Department of Health Sciences

INHS 3348.name: Database
INHS 3348.description: INHS 3348 Database Administration in Health Science This course examines the efficient use of data, information, and tools to securely manage, retrieve, and analyze healthcare data. Students will be introduced to the principles of computer science as well as database models and systems to provide proficiency in analytics. The course material will designate the standards and approaches underlying clinical data standards for use in clinical outcome support. Credits 3 Schedule Type Lecture Grading Basis Standard Letter (A-F) Administrative Unit Department of Health Sciences

INHS 4322.name: Concepts and
INHS 4322.description: INHS 4322 Concepts and Impacts of Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare This course gives an overview of the application of Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare. Through relevant case studies and videos, students will understand the strengths and weaknesses of AI applications. Also, ethical implications and potential biases of AI in Health care will be discussed. This course also gives insights into new opportunities to address healthcare needs with AI. Credits 3 Prerequisite Grade of "C" or better in INHS 1301 , INHS 2301 and Junior Classification. Schedule Type Lecture Grading Basis Standard Letter (A-F) Administrative Unit Department of Health Sciences
INHS 4322.prereq_raw: Grade of "C" or better in INHS 1301 , INHS 2301 and Junior Classification

INHS 4324.name: Applied
INHS 4324.description: INHS 4324 Applied Concepts of Public Health This course will provide a holistic review of the principles and practices of public health. Students will explore key concepts related to (i) determinants of health, disease, and injury (ii) Population health approach and health promotion (iii) tools of public health (iv) Public health institutions, and (iv) concepts of systems thinking and emerging global health issues. Credits 3 Prerequisite Grade of "C" or better in INHS 1301 and INHS 2301 . INHS 4324.prereq_raw: Grade of "C" or better in INHS 1301 and INHS 2301

INHS 4326.name: Evidence-Based
INHS 4326.description: INHS 4326 Evidence-Based Practices in Healthcare This course will provide a comprehensive overview of some of the most common evidence-based bundles and practices in healthcare, that create a strong foundation of practices. It will also cover some of the most common methodologies that allow practitioners and other staff to develop workflows based on evidence-based practices to reduce the number of medical errors in US Healthcare. The course will also cover how policies and procedures intervene in the evidence-based healthcare world and how regulations impact and regulate the evidence-based healthcare system to drive patient-centric care. Credits 3 Prerequisite Grade of "C" or better in INHS 4324 . Schedule Type Lecture Grading Basis Standard Letter (A-F) Administrative Unit Department of Health Sciences Offered As Scheduled
INHS 4326.prereq_raw: Grade of "C" or better in INHS 4324

INHS 4328.description: INHS 4328 Theory and Context of Epidemiology This course will provide an overview of epidemiological principles, practices, and their applications. INHS 4349.name: Clinical
INHS 4349.description: INHS 4349 Clinical Information Systems This course examines the role and function of clinical information systems and how they improve patient health and staff engagement. As health care and public health continue to evolve, the field of Clinical Information Systems has revealed an overwhelming universe of new, emerging, competing, and conflicting technologies and services. We continue to explore methods and techniques that structure healthcare workflows in a system using clinical information systems. It articulates intricate concepts for clinical information systems, providing a thorough yet unintimidating introduction to this complex and fascinating field.
